Tagcast 0.42.0 adds new ways to discover your collection, understand each page and
compare duplicate uploads before cleaning up. All features are included in the
standalone downloads for macOS, Windows and Linux.

## 1001 Albums: discover the albums you already own

- Enable **1001 Albums** in **Settings → Discovery**, then choose **Analyse my library**.
  The optional page compares the cleaned 1,001-album selection with your loaded
  library metadata. Opening the page never starts an analysis.
- Browse found, possible and missing matches; filter by decade, search and sort
  by release year. Confirm a possible match or choose your library edition manually.
  Account-scoped results and manual links are saved locally, without editing iBroadcast.
- Open a confirmed match for **About this album**, with an offline background text,
  Wikipedia attribution and CC BY-SA license link. All 1,001 entries have a text.
- The selection credits *1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die*, edited by
  Robert Dimery. Missing entries use grey, softened placeholder covers.
- **Show matching details** hides status/link controls when you want a quieter page.
  Its choice survives restarts and changes of local port or browser.

## Compare duplicate uploads before removing copies

- **Duplicate tracks** now finds repeated positive track numbers on the same disc,
  including different title/version text. **Duplicated** appears on album cards,
  list rows and the affected track titles. Separate discs remain separate.
- **Move to trash…** shows upload dates/times, date/format groups and suggested
  keep/trash labels. The preference is **FLAC over MP3**, then **the newest upload
  within the same format**. Different artists or clearly different durations,
  unknown formats and unresolved upload ties remain for manual comparison.
- **Select suggested copies** fills the checkboxes explicitly. Adjust the selection,
  review the exact tracks, then confirm. The original **Select extra copies** action
  retains its stricter title match and keeps the first copy.
- Suggestions compare stored metadata, not audio identity or recording quality.
  Tagcast only moves confirmed tracks to iBroadcast's trash; it never deletes permanently.

## Help and browsing

- A compact **?** starts a step-by-step tour for the current page or editor.
  Tours explain the screen without starting playback, analysis or saves.
- Settings can hide optional sidebar shortcuts, change their order and restore defaults.
  Connection controls, Settings and essential pages stay reachable.
- The Decades overview drops unnecessary sort/page controls. Opening a decade shows
  a short introduction to its music, alongside your random album selection.

## Downloads and updating

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.42.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.42.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.42.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.42.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Each archive includes Python, dependencies, the desktop launcher, a separate CLI,
license notices and a companion SHA-256 checksum. Album texts and their license
notice are bundled locally. Existing connections, settings and saved manual links remain.

**Stop the old Tagcast before starting 0.42.0.** Otherwise the new launcher opens
the already-running server. Settings remain in `~/.tagcast/`, or `TAGCAST_HOME`.
Source installations continue to support Python 3.11+ or uv.

For Homebrew, stop Tagcast, then run `brew update` and
`brew upgrade --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/tagcast` after the tap update is available.

See the [README](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.42.0/README.md)
and [standalone guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.42.0/docs/native-builds.md).
Your local music files are never changed.
